output.summary: The FY2026 record is mostly a commodity price effect. Bushels fell 0.9%, handling revenue was flat, and the cooperative ranked mid-pack against peers who adopted no program. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance cut 32%, while the deferred backlog tripled and the GM's incentive rewards the metric. Harlan Junction has insurer-confirmed dust and monitoring hazards, and an uninvestigated overheated-bearing near-miss. Drying and grading know-how sits with one near-retirement superintendent, undocumented. The expansion proposal rests on peak prices, unsourced throughput and no staffing or maintenance plan. Fix the hazards, capture knowledge, and defer the vote until the case is rebuilt on normalized prices. Do not freeze maintenance.
